# Localize a product for a new market

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

Before committing to a commercial launch in a market with different user, language or operating needs. A tested localized offer with approved market-entry requirements, support and a controlled launch decision.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

> Editorial status: operational draft. Source pages checked on 2026-10-29. No case-specific legal review, professional assurance or completed execution is claimed.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Research the market and target user journeys

agent-runnable


Collect evidence on demand, language, purchasing, payments, accessibility and support expectations. Identify how the proposed market differs from current operations without assuming translation alone establishes product fit.

- Sources: [International Trade Administration export roadmap](https://www.trade.gov/learn-how-export) · [W3C planning and managing web accessibility](https://www.w3.org/WAI/planning-and-managing/)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Review commercial and local requirements

human · human approval required


Product and qualified legal, tax and security owners assess the actual offer, customer terms, data flows and regulated uses. Assign unresolved licensing, entity, employment or export questions to their specialist processes.

- Sources: [International Trade Administration export roadmap](https://www.trade.gov/learn-how-export) · [W3C planning and managing web accessibility](https://www.w3.org/WAI/planning-and-managing/)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Prepare the localized product and operating plan

agent-runnable


Adapt content, formats, documentation, support and commercial configuration using reviewed terminology. Track integrations, pricing and fulfillment changes and keep unsupported promises out of marketing.

- Sources: [International Trade Administration export roadmap](https://www.trade.gov/learn-how-export) · [W3C planning and managing web accessibility](https://www.w3.org/WAI/planning-and-managing/)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Test with representative local users

human · human approval required


Run critical onboarding, product, payment, accessibility and support journeys with authorized test data. Capture defects and comprehension problems and confirm readiness against agreed acceptance criteria.

- Sources: [International Trade Administration export roadmap](https://www.trade.gov/learn-how-export) · [W3C planning and managing web accessibility](https://www.w3.org/WAI/planning-and-managing/)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Approve a bounded launch and monitor outcomes

human · human approval required


The accountable owners verify required approvals and operating capacity, then authorize the launch scope. Monitor customer outcomes and incidents and assign owners for changes before broad expansion.

- Verify: A tested localized offer with approved market-entry requirements, support and a controlled launch decision.
- Sources: [International Trade Administration export roadmap](https://www.trade.gov/learn-how-export) · [W3C planning and managing web accessibility](https://www.w3.org/WAI/planning-and-managing/)
